summary: This Cancer.Net (ASCO) article explains immunotherapy, a cancer treatment that uses substances made by the body or in a laboratory to boost the immune system and help it find and destroy cancer cells. It describes the main types: monoclonal antibodies and immune checkpoint inhibitors, non-specific immunotherapies (cytokines and BCG), oncolytic virus therapy, T-cell therapy, and cancer vaccines. It also lists questions patients can ask their health care team.
one_line: Cancer.Net overview of immunotherapy types, including checkpoint inhibitors, cytokines, BCG, oncolytic viruses, CAR T-cell therapy and cancer vaccines.
key_facts: Immunotherapy is a type of cancer treatment that uses substances made by the body or in a laboratory to boost the immune system.
Immunotherapy can be used alone or in combination with chemotherapy and/or other cancer treatments.
Checkpoint inhibitors commonly affect the PD-1/PD-L1 and CTLA-4 pathways.
Examples of immune checkpoint inhibitors listed include atezolizumab (Tecentriq), nivolumab (Opdivo) and pembrolizumab (Keytruda).
Pembrolizumab (Keytruda) is approved to treat tumors anywhere in the body with microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) or DNA mismatch repair deficiency (dMMR).
Interferon alpha is the most common interferon used in cancer treatment.
Interleukin-2 (IL-2), also called aldesleukin (Proleukin), can treat kidney cancer and melanoma.
Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) is placed directly into the bladder through a catheter to treat bladder cancer.
Talimogene laherparepvec (Imlygic) or T-VEC is a modified herpes simplex virus approved to treat advanced melanoma that cannot be treated with surgery.
In T-cell therapy, T cells are removed from the blood, given receptors that recognize cancer cells, and returned to the body; this is called chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy.
CAR T-cell therapy is used to treat certain blood cancers.
Gardasil is a cancer prevention vaccine that protects against the human papillomavirus (HPV).
Spuleucel-T (Provenge) is a treatment vaccine for advanced prostate cancer that does not respond to hormone therapy.
The article was approved by the Cancer.Net Editorial Board in 05/2022.
